summary: Armata Pharmaceuticals is a single-asset clinical-stage biotech dependent on FDA approval of phage therapy AP-SA02 and DoD funding. Its supply chain for custom phage manufacturing is narrow, and failure of either clinical or funding assumptions would destroy equity value.

inputs.fragility: High; proprietary, likely sole-source from CDMO

inputs.whyNeeded: Fermentation, purification, fill/finish for clinical and commercial supply
inputs.fragility: Medium; few qualified phage CDMOs, capacity constraints

inputs.whyNeeded: Growth of bacterial hosts for phage production

chokepoints.why: No approved product; failure sinks company
Non-dilutive cash critical for runway; no visible alternative funding

chokepoints.node: FDA fast track but binary approval risk
chokepoints.why: Precedent for phage approval is thin; clinical trial outcome binary

customers.why: Primary funder and potential early adopter for antibiotic-resistant infections

customers.node: Civilian patients with resistant Staph infections
customers.why: Broader downstream demand if market adoption grows

geographic: US-centric: FDA jurisdiction, DoD funding, clinical trial sites. No disclosed ex-US supply base.
substitutes: Traditional antibiotics (vancomycin, daptomycin) for Staph infections
Other late-stage antibiotic candidates (Paratek, Nabriva, etc.)
Next-gen phage therapeutics from competitors (Locus, BiomX, Adaptive Phage)

bearCase: AP-SA02 fails in Phase 3 or gets CRL; stock goes to near-zero.
DoD funding ends or is delayed; cash burn forces dilutive financing at low prices.
Phage manufacturing CDMO fails quality/commercial scaling; delays launch.
Market adoption for phage therapy is negligible; no revenue for years even if approved.

loadBearing.assumption: AP-SA02 receives FDA approval within 2 years
loadBearing.breaksIf: Phase 3 misses endpoint, CRL, or safety signal

loadBearing.assumption: DoD continues funding at current or higher levels
loadBearing.breaksIf: Budget cuts, lost contract, or protest

loadBearing.assumption: Manufacturing CDMO capacity is available and reliable
loadBearing.breaksIf: CDMO fails audit, capacity seized by larger client, or phage yield issues

loadBearing.assumption: Market adoption for phage therapy grows as antibiotic resistance worsens
loadBearing.breaksIf: Physician reluctance, payer non-coverage, or alternative antibiotics prevail

prediction.statement: AP-SA02 Phase 3 primary endpoint readout within 12 months, with top-line data by mid-2027.
prediction.resolutionCriterion: Company announces top-line Phase 3 results for AP-SA02, meeting or missing primary endpoint.

gaps: No public details on CDMO identity or capacity guarantees.
No disclosure of full clinical trial enrollment timeline or interim analyses.
No details on pricing/reimbursement strategy for AP-SA02.
No competitor phage pipeline maturity direct comparison.
verifyThese: Verify CDMO contract terms and exclusivity for AP-SA02 manufacturing.
Confirm DoD funding contract renewal date and total committed amounts.
Check FDA precedents for phage therapy approvals and agency feedback.
Assess cash runway: current burn rate and equity offering risk.
diminishingReturns: Stopped at phage manufacturing and DoD funding as deepest nodes; further hops (fermentation media suppliers, steel for bioreactors) are generic bioprocess inputs with ample substitutes and no material fragility for this micro-cap.
